title: CBSE CLASS 11 — Biology | Plant Kingdom Algae Bryophytes Pteridophytes
description: Subject-wise test on Plant Kingdom Algae Bryophytes Pteridophytes (Biology) for CBSE CLASS 11. 50Q.
subject: cbse11-biology
instructions: Topic: Plant Kingdom Algae Bryophytes Pteridophytes

questions.question: Which of the following pigments is found in all classes of Algae?

options.explanation: Fucoxanthin is a pigment characteristic of brown algae (Phaeophyceae).
Phycoerythrin is a pigment found in red algae (Rhodophyceae).
Chlorophyll a is the primary photosynthetic pigment present in all photosynthetic eukaryotic organisms, including all classes of algae.
Carotenoids are accessory pigments and are not always the primary photosynthetic pigment.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll 'a' is the primary photosynthetic pigment found universally in all photosynthetic eukaryotic organisms, including all classes of algae (Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae). Fucoxanthin is characteristic of brown algae, phycoerythrin of red algae, and carotenoids are accessory pigments, not always the primary one.
questions.hint: Consider the primary photosynthetic pigment in all photosynthetic organisms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The dominant phase in the life cycle of a Bryophyte is the:

options.explanation: The sporophyte is short-lived and dependent on the gametophyte.
The gametophyte is the dominant, independent phase in Bryophytes.
Protonema is an early stage of the gametophyte in mosses.
Prothallus is a term used for the gametophyte of Pteridophytes.

questions.explanation: Bryophytes have a dominant, independent, photosynthetic thalloid or erect gametophyte. The sporophyte is short-lived and totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte for its nutrition and anchorage.
questions.hint: Focus on the phase that is independent and photosynthetic in Bryophytes.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a colonial green alga?

options.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga.
Chlamydomonas is a unicellular green alga.
Volvox forms spherical colonies and is a colonial green alga.
Ulothrix is a filamentous green alga.

questions.explanation: Volvox is a well-known example of a colonial green alga, forming spherical colonies. Spirogyra and Ulothrix are filamentous, while Chlamydomonas is a unicellular alga.
questions.hint: Look for a green alga that forms colonies.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Pteridophytes are often referred to as:

options.explanation: Pteridophytes have vascular tissues.
Pteridophytes are vascular plants that reproduce by spores (cryptogams).
Phanerogams are seed-producing plants.
Pteridophytes do not produce seeds.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) but they do not produce seeds, instead reproducing by spores. Hence, they are called vascular cryptogams (cryptogams meaning plants without seeds or flowers).
questions.hint: Consider the defining characteristics of Pteridophytes: vascular tissues but no seeds.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: In most mosses, the sex organs (antheridia and archegonia) are produced:

options.explanation: The sporophyte is the dependent phase in mosses.

options.text: At the apex of leafy gametophyte shoots
options.explanation: The antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy gametophyte shoots.
The protonema is an early stage of the gametophyte.
Rhizoids are for anchorage, not for producing sex organs.

questions.explanation: In mosses, the dominant phase is the leafy gametophyte. The antheridia (male sex organs) and archegonia (female sex organs) are typically produced at the apex of these leafy gametophyte shoots.
questions.hint: Focus on the dominant phase of mosses and where their sex organs are located.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly represents a homosporous pteridophyte and a heterosporous pteridophyte, respectively?

options.explanation: Both are heterosporous pteridophytes.
Both are homosporous pteridophytes.
Lycopodium is homosporous, and Selaginella is heterosporous.
Salvinia is heterosporous, and Equisetum is homosporous.

questions.explanation: Homosporous pteridophytes produce only one type of spore, while heterosporous pteridophytes produce two different types of spores (microspores and megaspores). Lycopodium and Equisetum are examples of homosporous pteridophytes. Selaginella and Salvinia are examples of heterosporous pteridophytes. Therefore, Lycopodium (homosporous) and Selaginella (heterosporous) is the correct pair.
questions.hint: Identify the homosporous and heterosporous pteridophytes from the given options.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A unique characteristic of Rhodophyceae (red algae) that differentiates them from other algal groups is:

options.text: Presence of chlorophyll a and b
options.explanation: Chlorophyll a and b are found in green algae.
Mannitol storage is characteristic of brown algae.

options.text: Absence of flagellated stages in their life cycle
options.explanation: Red algae lack flagellated stages, including gametes, which is unique among algae.
Fucoxanthin is a pigment found in brown algae.

questions.explanation: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) are unique among the algal groups because they completely lack flagellated stages in any part of their life cycle, including gametes. Chlorophyll a and b are characteristic of green algae, mannitol storage is for brown algae, and fucoxanthin is also for brown algae.
questions.hint: Consider the unique feature of red algae that sets them apart from other algae.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Consider the following characteristics: I. Plant body is thalloid, lacks true roots, stem, and leaves. II. Possesses rhizoids for anchorage. III. Dependent on water for fertilization. IV. Sporophyte is parasitic on the gametophyte. These characteristics are typical of which plant group?

options.explanation: Algae have simpler plant bodies and do not have a parasitic sporophyte.
The characteristics match Bryophytes, which have a thalloid or leafy gametophyte, rhizoids, water-dependent fertilization, and a parasitic sporophyte.
Pteridophytes have true roots, stems, leaves, and independent sporophytes.
Gymnosperms are seed-producing plants with a dominant sporophyte.

questions.explanation: The description perfectly fits Bryophytes. Their plant body is thalloid or leafy, attached by rhizoids, and they are dependent on water for the movement of sperm to the egg. Critically, their sporophyte is nutritionally dependent on the gametophyte. Algae are simpler, Pteridophytes have true roots/stem/leaves and independent sporophytes, and Gymnosperms are seed-bearing plants.
questions.hint: Analyze the given characteristics and match them with the plant group they describe.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom. Reason (R): They live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true; bryophytes are indeed called amphibians of the plant kingdom. The reason provided is also true, as they require a film of water for the transfer of antherozoids (male gametes) to the archegonium (female sex organ) for fertilization. This dependence on water for reproduction, despite living on land, is precisely why they are termed 'amphibians.' Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Evaluate both the assertion and reason to determine if the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Pteridophytes?

options.explanation: Bryophytes have a dominant gametophyte, not Pteridophytes.
Pteridophytes reproduce by spores, not seeds. Gymnosperms reproduce by seeds.

options.text: Possesses true roots, stem, and leaves
options.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to have true roots, stems, and leaves.
Pteridophytes possess well-differentiated vascular tissues.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are vascular plants that reproduce via spores and possess true roots, stems, and leaves. They have a dominant sporophyte and a small, often photosynthetic gametophyte.
questions.hint: Consider the plant groups mentioned and their reproductive methods.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The gametophyte in Pteridophytes is typically ______.

options.explanation: The gametophyte in Bryophytes is large and photosynthetic, not in Pteridophytes.
Pteridophytes have a small, often photosynthetic gametophyte called a prothallus.
The dominant phase in Pteridophytes is the sporophyte, not the gametophyte.
The gametophyte in Pteridophytes is usually above ground and photosynthetic.

questions.explanation: In Pteridophytes, the gametophyte is usually small, inconspicuous, and often photosynthetic. It is independent and often referred to as a prothallus.
questions.hint: Think about the size and visibility of the gametophyte in Pteridophytes.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which plant group is the first terrestrial plant to possess vascular tissues?

options.explanation: Bryophytes lack true vascular tissues and rely on diffusion for water and nutrient transport.
Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess true vascular tissues.
Algae are non-vascular aquatic plants.
Gymnosperms have vascular tissues but are not the first terrestrial plants to possess them.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are considered the first terrestrial plants to have well-differentiated vascular tissues, enabling them to transport water and nutrients efficiently.
questions.hint: Consider the evolutionary development of vascular tissues in plants.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following classes of Algae is characterized by the presence of fucoxanthin as the major accessory pigment and stored food in the form of laminarin or mannitol?

options.explanation: Chlorophyceae store starch as food.
Phaeophyceae store food as laminarin or mannitol and contain fucoxanthin.
Rhodophyceae store floridean starch as food.
Cyanophyceae are blue-green algae and do not store laminarin or mannitol.

questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae (brown algae) are characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and fucoxanthin. Their food is stored as laminarin or mannitol. Chlorophyceae store starch, and Rhodophyceae store floridean starch.
questions.hint: This class is commonly known as brown algae.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Bryophytes are often referred to as the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" because:

options.text: They can live in soil but depend on water for vegetative reproduction.
options.explanation: Bryophytes depend on water for sexual reproduction, not vegetative reproduction.

options.text: They can live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction.
options.explanation: Bryophytes require water for fertilization (sexual reproduction).

options.text: They can live in water but depend on soil for vegetative reproduction.
options.explanation: This is not a defining characteristic of bryophytes.

options.text: They can live in water but depend on soil for sexual reproduction.
options.explanation: Bryophytes require water, not soil, for sexual reproduction.

questions.explanation: Bryophytes require water for the transfer of antherozoids (male gametes) to the archegonium (female sex organ) for fertilization. Hence, they are dependent on water for sexual reproduction, even though they live in terrestrial habitats.
questions.hint: Amphibians live both in water and on land.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) are:

options.explanation: Algae are non-vascular plants.
Bryophytes lack true vascular tissues.
Pteridophytes are the first vascular plants.
Gymnosperms are vascular but not the first.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first group of terrestrial plants to evolve a vascular system, which includes xylem for water conduction and phloem for food conduction, allowing them to grow taller and colonize land more effectively than bryophytes.
questions.hint: These plants have true roots, stems, and leaves.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly known as "peat moss"?

options.explanation: Sphagnum is the correct answer.
Funaria is a genus of mosses but not peat moss.
Marchantia is a liverwort, not moss.
Polytrichum is a moss but not peat moss.

questions.explanation: Sphagnum is a genus of mosses widely known as peat moss. It has great water-holding capacity and is used as packing material for trans-shipment of living material and in nurseries.
questions.hint: This moss is used in gardening and horticulture.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Observe the following characteristics: I. Presence of chlorophyll a and b. II. Stored food is starch. III. Cell wall made of cellulose. IV. Usually possess two to eight, equal, apical flagella. These characteristics are typical for members of which algal class?

options.explanation: Phaeophyceae have chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin.
Rhodophyceae have chlorophyll a, phycobilins, and store floridean starch.
Chlorophyceae have chlorophyll a, b, store starch, and have cellulose cell walls.
Cyanophyceae are blue-green algae without cellulose cell walls.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae (green algae) are characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a and b, stored food as starch, and a cell wall primarily composed of cellulose. Most of them have 2-8, equal, apical flagella, as seen in Chlamydomonas and Volvox.
questions.hint: This class is known as green algae.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the life cycle of a plant: 1. The dominant phase is the gametophyte. 2. The sporophyte is completely dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition. 3. Rhizoids are present for anchorage. 4. Antherozoids require water for transfer to the archegonium. Based on these statements, identify the group of plants described.

options.explanation: Algae do not have rhizoids or a dominant gametophyte phase like bryophytes.
Bryophytes have all the described characteristics.
Pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte and independent gametophyte.
Gymnosperms are seed plants with dominant sporophytes.

questions.explanation: The described characteristics—dominant gametophyte, sporophyte dependent on gametophyte, presence of rhizoids, and requirement of water for fertilization—are all hallmark features of Bryophytes (e.g., mosses and liverworts).
questions.hint: These plants lack true vascular tissues.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following pteridophytes exhibits heterospory?

options.explanation: Lycopodium is generally homosporous, producing only one type of spore.
Equisetum is homosporous, producing only one type of spore.
Selaginella is heterosporous, producing both microspores and megaspores.
Adiantum is homosporous, producing only one type of spore.

questions.explanation: Heterospory is the production of two different types of spores (microspores and megaspores). Among the given options, Selaginella is a well-known example of a heterosporous pteridophyte.
questions.hint: Consider pteridophytes known for producing two types of spores.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following pigments is characteristic of members belonging to Phaeophyceae (brown algae)?

options.explanation: Phycoerythrin is a red pigment found in Rhodophyceae (red algae).
Chlorophyll a is present in all photosynthetic plants, but Phaeophyceae also have chlorophyll c.
Fucoxanthin is the dominant xanthophyll pigment in Phaeophyceae.
While xanthophylls are present, fucoxanthin is the specific and dominant pigment.

questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae, or brown algae, are characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and the dominant xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin, which gives them their characteristic brown colour.
questions.hint: Fucoxanthin is a xanthophyll pigment that imparts a brown colour to these algae.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Why are Bryophytes often referred to as the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'?

options.text: They can live both in water and on land.
options.explanation: While they can survive in both environments, the key reason for the term 'amphibians' is their reproductive dependence on water.

options.text: They live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction.
options.explanation: This is the defining characteristic that earns them the title 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'.

options.text: Their gametophytes are aquatic while sporophytes are terrestrial.
options.explanation: Bryophytes do not have distinct aquatic gametophytes and terrestrial sporophytes.

options.text: They have both vascular and non-vascular tissues.
options.explanation: Bryophytes lack vascular tissues entirely.

questions.explanation: Bryophytes require water for the movement of male gametes (antherozoids) to the archegonium for fertilization, even though they can grow on land. This dependence on water for reproduction, despite living on land, earns them the title.
questions.hint: Think about their reproductive process and environment.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a homosporous pteridophyte?

options.explanation: Selaginella is a heterosporous pteridophyte.
Salvinia is a heterosporous pteridophyte.
Dryopteris is a homosporous pteridophyte.
Both Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous.

questions.explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous pteridophytes, producing two different types of spores (microspores and megaspores). Dryopteris (fern) is a homosporous pteridophyte, producing only one type of spore.
questions.hint: Homosporous pteridophytes produce only one type of spore.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The main plant body of a Pteridophyte is a:

options.explanation: The gametophyte is haploid but not the dominant phase.
Pteridophytes do not have a diploid gametophyte.
The sporophyte is the dominant diploid phase in pteridophytes.
The sporophyte is diploid, not haploid.

questions.explanation: In Pteridophytes, the dominant phase in the life cycle is the diploid sporophyte, which is differentiated into true roots, stem, and leaves. The gametophyte is small and inconspicuous.
questions.hint: The dominant phase in the life cycle of pteridophytes is diploid and sporophytic.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the prothallus of a fern (Pteridophyte) is correct?

options.text: It is the dominant sporophytic phase.
options.explanation: The prothallus is the gametophyte, not the sporophyte.

options.text: It is a parasitic structure on the sporophyte.
options.explanation: The prothallus is free-living and not parasitic.

options.text: It is a diploid structure that produces spores.
options.explanation: The prothallus is haploid and produces gametes, not spores.

options.text: It is a free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of the prothallus.

questions.explanation: The prothallus is the small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte of pteridophytes. It bears sex organs (antheridia and archegonia) and produces gametes.
questions.hint: The prothallus is a gametophyte that is free-living and photosynthetic.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Red algae are able to grow in deeper waters than other algae. Reason (R): Red algae possess the pigment phycoerythrin, which can absorb blue-green light that penetrates deeper into the water.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Red algae contain the pigment phycoerythrin, which is efficient at absorbing blue-green wavelengths of light. Blue-green light penetrates deeper into water, allowing red algae to photosynthesize effectively at greater depths where other pigments might not be as efficient.
questions.hint: Think about the role of pigments in light absorption and depth of water.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Identify the incorrect match from the following:

options.explanation: Volvox is correctly matched as a colonial alga.
Ulothrix is correctly matched as a filamentous alga.
Fucus is multicellular, not unicellular.
Spirogyra is correctly matched as a filamentous alga.

questions.explanation: Volvox is a colonial green alga, Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous green algae. Fucus is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae) that is multicellular and branched, not unicellular.
questions.hint: Fucus is a brown alga and is multicellular.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: These features are characteristic of which algal group? I. Presence of chlorophyll a and b II. Storage of food as starch III. Cell wall made of cellulose IV. Motile flagellated gametes

options.explanation: Phaeophyceae (brown algae) have chlorophyll a and c, store food as laminarin, and have cell walls with algin.
Chlorophyceae (green algae) have these characteristics.
Rhodophyceae (red algae) have chlorophyll a and d, store food as floridean starch, and have cell walls with agar and carrageenan.
Cyanophyceae (blue-green algae) are prokaryotic and lack chlorophyll b.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae (green algae) possess chlorophyll a and b, store food primarily as starch, have a cell wall made of cellulose, and often have motile flagellated gametes. These features are also shared with higher plants, suggesting an evolutionary link.
questions.hint: These features are typical of green algae.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Based on the description, to which group of the plant kingdom does this organism most likely belong?

options.explanation: Algae lack a distinct sporophyte phase.
Pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte and true vascular tissues.
The description matches bryophytes.
Gymnosperms are seed plants with vascular tissues.

questions.explanation: The description perfectly matches the characteristics of Bryophytes: a thalloid plant body lacking true roots/stems/leaves, a dominant free-living gametophyte, a dependent sporophyte, and a requirement for water for fertilization. Algae lack a distinct sporophyte, Pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte and true vascular tissues, and Gymnosperms are seed plants.
questions.hint: Consider the plant body structure, reproductive features, and environment.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the life cycle of Marchantia (a bryophyte) is correct?

options.text: The sporophyte is the dominant, free-living phase.
options.explanation: The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte.

options.text: Spores are produced by mitosis from the gametophyte.
options.explanation: Spores are produced by meiosis from the sporophyte.

options.text: Antheridiophores and archegoniophores are structures found on different thalli.
options.explanation: This is correct for Marchantia.

options.text: The zygote develops into a photosynthetic, independent sporophyte.
options.explanation: The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte.

questions.explanation: Marchantia is a dioecious bryophyte, meaning male (antheridiophore) and female (archegoniophore) reproductive structures are borne on separate thalli. The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte, and spores are produced by meiosis from the sporophyte, not mitosis from the gametophyte.
questions.hint: Marchantia is dioecious, with male and female structures on separate plants.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the plant with its group?

options.explanation: Incorrect match for Funaria (should be A, not 1-A).
Correct match: 1-B (Funaria - moss), 2-A (Marchantia - liverwort), 3-C (Selaginella - club moss), 4-D (Pinus - gymnosperm).
Incorrect match for Funaria (should be A, not 1-D).
Incorrect match for Funaria (should be A, not 1-A) and Selaginella (should be C, not 3-B).

questions.explanation: Funaria is a moss, Marchantia is a liverwort, Selaginella is a club moss, and Pinus is a gymnosperm.
questions.hint: Match the common names to their botanical groups.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The edible part of Laminaria (kelp) is rich in which nutrient?

options.explanation: Laminaria is not primarily a protein source.
Laminaria is a rich source of iodine, essential for thyroid function.
While seaweeds contain some vitamin C, it is not the primary nutrient in Laminaria.
Laminaria does not store starch as its primary nutrient.

questions.explanation: Laminaria is a brown alga known for its high iodine content, often used in dietary supplements.
questions.hint: Think about the nutritional benefits of seaweeds like kelp.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which group of the plant kingdom is characterized by a plant body differentiated into root-like, stem-like, and leaf-like structures that are not true organs, lacks vascular tissues, has a dominant and free-living gametophytic stage, and a short-lived dependent sporophytic stage?

options.explanation: Pteridophytes (ferns and their relatives) have vascular tissues and a dominant sporophyte stage.
Bryophytes match all the given features: non-vascular, dominant gametophyte, and dependent sporophyte.
Gymnosperms are seed-producing vascular plants with a dominant sporophyte stage.
Angiosperms are flowering plants with vascular tissues and a dominant sporophyte stage.

questions.explanation: This description matches the Bryophyta group, which includes mosses, liverworts, and hornworts. These plants exhibit a dominant gametophyte stage, lack vascular tissues (being non-vascular), and require a film of water for fertilization.
questions.hint: Consider non-vascular plants with a life cycle where the gametophyte is the dominant phase.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following pigments is found in all members of Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae?

options.explanation: Fucoxanthin is characteristic of Phaeophyceae (brown algae).
Phycoerythrin is characteristic of Rhodophyceae (red algae).
Chlorophyll b is characteristic of Chlorophyceae (green algae).
Chlorophyll a is present in all photosynthetic organisms, including Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a is a universal photosynthetic pigment found in all eukaryotic photosynthetic organisms, including all classes of algae. Fucoxanthin is characteristic of Phaeophyceae, Phycoerythrin of Rhodophyceae, and Chlorophyll b of Chlorophyceae.
questions.hint: Consider the primary photosynthetic pigment present in all photosynthetic organisms.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which class of algae is characterized by the presence of fucoxanthin as the major accessory pigment and stores food primarily as laminarin and mannitol?

options.explanation: Chlorophyceae (green algae) store starch and do not have fucoxanthin.
Rhodophyceae (red algae) store floridean starch and have phycoerythrin as the major pigment.
Cyanophyceae (blue-green algae) are prokaryotic and do not have fucoxanthin.
Phaeophyceae (brown algae) have fucoxanthin and store food as laminarin and mannitol.

questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae (brown algae) are characterized by the presence of fucoxanthin as the major accessory pigment, which gives them their characteristic brown colour, and they store food in the form of laminarin and mannitol. Chlorophyceae (green algae) store starch, and Rhodophyceae (red algae) store floridean starch.
questions.hint: This class is known for its brown color due to the pigment fucoxanthin.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It typically consists of:

options.explanation: Bryophytes do not have true roots, stems, or leaves; they have rhizoids instead.

options.text: Thallus-like and prostrate or erect structures
options.explanation: The plant body of bryophytes is typically thallus-like and can be prostrate or erect.
Bryophytes are multicellular organisms with a differentiated plant body.

options.text: Vascular tissues like xylem and phloem
options.explanation: Bryophytes lack vascular tissues; xylem and phloem are absent.

questions.explanation: Bryophytes have a thallus-like plant body, which can be prostrate or erect, and is more differentiated than algae. However, it lacks true roots, stem, or leaves, possessing root-like rhizoids instead.
questions.hint: Bryophytes lack true vascular tissues and have a simple body structure.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following plant groups is considered the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)?

options.explanation: Algae are non-vascular and typically aquatic.
Bryophytes lack vascular tissues and are non-vascular plants.
Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants with vascular tissues.
Gymnosperms are vascular but evolved after pteridophytes.

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to evolve and possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), which allowed them to grow taller and colonize land more effectively than non-vascular bryophytes and algae.
questions.hint: Look for the group that has true vascular tissues.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: In which of the following groups is the gametophyte independent and photosynthetic, while the sporophyte is completely or partially dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition?

options.explanation: In pteridophytes, the sporophyte is the dominant phase and is independent.
Gymnosperms have a dominant sporophyte stage, and the gametophyte is dependent.
Angiosperms also have a dominant sporophyte stage.
In bryophytes, the gametophyte is dominant and photosynthetic, while the sporophyte is dependent.

questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the dominant phase in the life cycle is the free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte. The sporophyte is smaller, short-lived, and remains attached to and dependent on the gametophyte for its nutrition.
questions.hint: Consider the life cycle where the gametophyte is the dominant stage.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A scientist observes an algal sample under a microscope and notes the presence of chlorophyll a and b, along with pyrenoids (storage bodies), and a rigid cell wall made of cellulose. The sample likely belongs to which class?

options.explanation: Phaeophyceae have chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin, not chlorophyll b.
Rhodophyceae have chlorophyll a, d, and phycoerythrin, not chlorophyll b.
Chlorophyceae have chlorophyll a and b, pyrenoids, and cellulose cell walls.
Cyanophyceae are prokaryotic and lack chlorophyll b.

questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae (green algae) are characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a and b (similar to higher plants), pyrenoids (associated with starch storage), and a cell wall primarily composed of cellulose. Phaeophyceae have chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin; Rhodophyceae have chlorophyll a, d, and phycoerythrin.
questions.hint: Look for the class of algae that has chlorophyll a and b and cellulose cell walls.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Sphagnum, a type of moss, is highly valued for its ability to absorb large quantities of water due to its unique cell structure. This property makes it particularly useful as:

options.explanation: Agar-agar is derived from red algae, not Sphagnum.
Sphagnum is not specifically used as an indicator of water pollution.

options.text: Packing material for trans-shipment of living material
options.explanation: Sphagnum's high water retention makes it ideal for packing living material.

options.text: A primary producer in deep-sea ecosystems
options.explanation: Sphagnum is a terrestrial plant and not found in deep-sea ecosystems.

questions.explanation: Sphagnum has specialized dead cells (hyaline cells) that can absorb and hold water up to 18 times its dry weight. This makes it an excellent packing material for keeping seedlings, cut flowers, and other living plant materials moist during transport. It is also used as peat.
questions.hint: Think about the practical uses of Sphagnum moss in horticulture and shipping.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Pteridophytes: I. Most pteridophytes are homosporous. II. Heterosporous pteridophytes produce two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores. III. Selaginella and Salvinia are examples of homosporous pteridophytes. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while statement III is incorrect.
Statement III is incorrect; Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous.
Statement III is incorrect; Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous.
Statement III is incorrect; the correct answer is I and II only.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: The majority of pteridophytes produce only one type of spore (homosporous). Statement II is correct: Heterosporous pteridophytes produce two distinct types of spores: microspores (which develop into male gametophytes) and megaspores (which develop into female gametophytes). Statement III is incorrect: Selaginella and Salvinia are classic examples of *heterosporous* pteridophytes, not homosporous.
questions.hint: Analyze each statement carefully, especially statement III, which is a common misconception.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): The antherozoids of bryophytes and pteridophytes require a film of water to reach the archegonia. Reason (R): Both bryophytes and pteridophytes have motile male gametes.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. The antherozoids (male gametes) of bryophytes and pteridophytes are flagellated and require water to swim to the archegonia for fertilization.
questions.hint: Understand the role of water in the fertilization process of these plants.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of algae that distinguishes them from bryophytes?

options.explanation: Both algae and bryophytes lack vascular tissues.
Both algae and bryophytes exhibit alternation of generations.
Algae contain chlorophyll-a and chlorophyll-b, while bryophytes lack chlorophyll-b.

options.text: Occurrence in both aquatic and terrestrial habitats
options.explanation: Most algae are aquatic, though some are terrestrial. Bryophytes are primarily terrestrial.

questions.explanation: Algae contain chlorophyll-a and chlorophyll-b as primary photosynthetic pigments, while bryophytes lack chlorophyll-b and have other accessory pigments. Vascular tissues are absent in both algae and bryophytes. Alternation of generations is seen in both algae and bryophytes. Though some algae are terrestrial, most are aquatic.
questions.hint: Consider the types of chlorophyll present in algae and bryophytes.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Identify the correct match between the group and its representative member:

options.explanation: Spirogyra belongs to Chlorophyta, but this is not the only or best match listed.
Chlamydomonas belongs to Chlorophyta, not Phaeophyta.
Fucus belongs to Phaeophyta, not Rhodophyta.
Marchantia is a well-known liverwort belonging to Bryophyta.

questions.explanation: Marchantia is a well-known liverwort belonging to Bryophyta. Spirogyra is a green alga (Chlorophyta), Chlamydomonas is a green alga (Chlorophyta), and Fucus is a brown alga (Phaeophyta). Rhodophyta includes red algae like Polysiphonia, not Fucus.
questions.hint: Match the group names with their well-known members.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Ulothrix is a filamentous green alga commonly found in freshwater. Reason (R): It reproduces asexually by fragmentation and sexually by isogamy or anisogamy.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Ulothrix is indeed a filamentous green alga found in freshwater. It reproduces asexually via fragmentation and sexually through isogamy or anisogamy, making the assertion and reason both correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Analyze whether the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the sporophyte in the life cycle of a moss?

options.text: It is diploid and dependent on the gametophyte
options.explanation: This is a correct feature of the sporophyte in mosses.

options.text: It bears a capsule where meiosis occurs
options.explanation: This is a correct feature of the sporophyte in mosses.
The sporophyte does not produce gametes; the gametophyte does.

options.text: It develops from the zygote after fertilization
options.explanation: This is a correct feature of the sporophyte in mosses.

questions.explanation: The sporophyte in mosses is diploid, dependent on the gametophyte, produces spores via meiosis in the capsule, and develops from the zygote. It does not produce gametes; gametes are produced by the gametophyte through mitosis.
questions.hint: Focus on the functions of the sporophyte stage in mosses.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A student observed a plant growing in a moist, shaded area with leafy structures and rhizoids but no true roots or vascular tissues. The plant likely belongs to which group?

options.explanation: Algae lack leafy structures and rhizoids.
Bryophytes like mosses have leafy structures, rhizoids, and lack vascular tissues.
Pteridophytes have true roots and vascular tissues.
Gymnosperms have true roots and vascular tissues.

questions.explanation: The presence of leafy structures and rhizoids (not true roots), along with the lack of vascular tissues and occurrence in moist, shaded areas, is characteristic of bryophytes such as mosses.
questions.hint: Consider the presence or absence of vascular tissues and true roots.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following algae groups is primarily marine and contains pigments like phycoerythrin and phycocyanin?

options.explanation: Chlorophyta are green algae with chlorophylls a and b.
Phaeophyta are brown algae with pigments like fucoxanthin.
Rhodophyta are red algae with phycoerythrin and phycocyanin.
Xanthophyta are yellow-green algae.

questions.explanation: Rhodophyta (red algae) are primarily marine, contain phycoerythrin and phycocyanin, and are adapted to deep-water environments. Chlorophyta are green algae, Phaeophyta are brown algae, and Xanthophyta are yellow-green algae.
questions.hint: Look for the group known for red pigments and primarily marine habitat.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: In the life cycle of a typical pteridophyte, the dominant phase is:

options.explanation: The gametophyte is reduced and short-lived in pteridophytes.
The sporophyte is the dominant phase in pteridophytes.
The prothallus is the gametophyte, which is reduced.
The zygote develops into the sporophyte.

questions.explanation: In pteridophytes, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, conspicuous phase, while the haploid gametophyte is reduced and short-lived. The prothallus is the gametophyte in ferns, and the zygote develops into the sporophyte.
questions.hint: Consider which phase is more prominent and long-lived in pteridophytes.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: What is the main difference between the life cycles of algae and bryophytes?

options.text: Algae exhibit alternation of generations, while bryophytes do not
options.explanation: Both algae and bryophytes exhibit alternation of generations.

options.text: Bryophytes have a dominant gametophyte, while algae have a dominant sporophyte
options.explanation: This is the main difference between their life cycles.

options.text: Algae reproduce only asexually, while bryophytes reproduce only sexually
options.explanation: Algae can reproduce both sexually and asexually.

options.text: Bryophytes have vascular tissues, while algae do not
options.explanation: Both algae and bryophytes lack vascular tissues.

questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the haploid gametophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic phase, while in most algae, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant phase. Both groups exhibit alternation of generations, algae are not exclusively asexual, and bryophytes lack vascular tissues.
questions.hint: Compare the dominant phases in the life cycles of algae and bryophytes.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology

questions.question: A student observes a plant body that is thalloid, dorsiventral, and lacks true roots but has unicellular rhizoids. It also produces gemmae for vegetative reproduction. Identify the plant.

options.explanation: Marchantia fits the description with a thalloid, dorsiventral body and reproduces via gemmae.
Funaria has multicellular rhizoids, not unicellular.
Selaginella has true roots.
Spirogyra is filamentous and lacks a thalloid structure.

questions.explanation: Marchantia is a liverwort with a thalloid, dorsiventral plant body, unicellular rhizoids, and reproduces vegetatively via gemmae. Funaria is a moss with multicellular rhizoids, Selaginella is a pteridophyte with true roots, and Spirogyra is a filamentous alga.
questions.hint: Consider the structure and reproductive method of the plant.
questions.subject: cbse11-biology
